overall: Every source URL resolved and every licence and may_publish claim matched the source (Commons extmetadata, Met, AIC, Cleveland and Smithsonian records), so licence accuracy did not separate the two; both flagged CC BY-SA share-alike and personality rights where they applied. The difference was fit: X more often found an image that literally contains the brief (a seeded loaf among pale ones, a crowded church choir, a portrait lighthouse, Lagos traffic), while Y was stronger on pure compositional metaphors (perspective roads, river confluences, near-empty nocturnes). Y sometimes offered a layout analogy from an unrelated subject (sneakers) or a weaker second pick (keyboard, Redon urn). Reasoning quality was similar and mostly concrete on both sides; X lost a point for admitting it chose one image unseen, and Y missed that its sockeye image is too small for a cover.
